group: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love? + Another Century's Episode 2 originals

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Protagonist of Macross DYRL; former civilian stunt flyer turned U.N. Spacy VF-1 Valkyrie pilot (Skull Squadron).
entries.personality: Hot-headed, impulsive and stubborn young pilot who grows into responsibility; caught in a love triangle between Minmay and Misa.
entries.notes: Macross wiki page title is 'Hikaru Ichijyo' (AnimEigo/official spelling); 'Hikaru Ichijo' redirects there and is the ADV subtitle spelling. Akurasu lists him as 'Ichijo Hikaru' (Japanese order). Use Ichijyo.

entries.ja: マクシミリアン・ジーナス
entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: U.N. Spacy ace VF-1 pilot, Hikaru's wingman in Skull Squadron.
entries.personality: Calm, cheerful, unflappable prodigy pilot; later falls for and marries the Meltran ace Milia.
entries.notes: Wiki page title 'Maximilian Jenius', commonly called 'Max' (also alias 'Max Jenius').

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Skull Squadron leader, veteran ace VF-1S pilot and Hikaru's senpai/mentor.
entries.personality: Brave, easygoing 'man's man' and ladies' man; rough exterior hiding compassion and humor even in grim situations.
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Roy Focker' (official Big West spelling). Variants: 'Roy Fokker' (Akurasu ACE2 database, Robotech), 'Roy Foecker' (umlaut form on en.wikipedia). Use Focker.

entries.ja: ミリア・ファリーナ・ジーナス
entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Meltrandi (female Zentradi) ace pilot of the Queadluun-Rau; rival and later wife of Max.
entries.personality: Proud, fiercely competitive warrior obsessed with being the best; falls for Max after he defeats her.
entries.notes: CONTESTED. Macross wiki page TITLE is 'Milia Farina Jenius', but the same page's body/infobox and Max's page use 'Milia Fallyna Jenius' (the official Big West / Macross Compendium form). Akurasu uses 'Millia Farina Jenius'. Robotech uses 'Miriya'. Per 'wiki wins' (page title) the default is 'Milia Farina Jenius'; 'Milia Fallyna Jenius' is an equally defensible official alternative. Short name 'Milia' (not 'Millia'). In DYRL proper she is named 'Milia 639' (see separate entry); the full married name is used in-game here.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Same character as Milia Farina Jenius; her DYRL-era Meltran designation before joining the humans.
entries.notes: Macross wiki lists 'Milia 639' as her DYRL alias. Game uses both ミリア639 and ミリア labels; keep the number when the label carries it.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: U.N. Spacy officer (Lieutenant), bridge officer/coordinator of the SDF-1 Macross.
entries.personality: Stern, by-the-book, duty-bound officer with little humor at work; softens and grows close to Hikaru.
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Misa Hayase' (married name Misa Ichijyo later; not relevant here). Robotech 'Lisa Hayes' must not be used.

entries.ja: ブルーノ・Ｊ・グローバル
entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Captain of the SDF-1 Macross (U.N. Spacy).
entries.personality: Calm, old-fashioned veteran commander with a broad strategic view; pipe smoker who dislikes the spotlight.
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Bruno J. Global'. Short label 'Global' (or 'Capt. Global' if space allows).

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: SDF-1 Macross bridge operator (one of the three bridge operators with Vanessa and Shammy).
entries.personality: Boyish, forward and gossipy; teases the younger Shammy.
entries.notes: Identified as Kim Kabirov (キム・キャビロフ), wiki title 'Kim Kabirov'. The game only uses 'キム', so 'Kim' is safe; use 'Kim Kabirov' only if a full name is needed. Caveat: the wiki notes DYRL's credits swapped Kim's and Shammy's names by error, so the on-screen DYRL 'Kim' identity is slightly muddled; the label 'Kim' itself is not in doubt.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Zentradi fleet commander under the Boddole Zer Main Fleet; pursues and later allies with the Macross.
entries.personality: Massive, tenacious, honorable veteran warrior; pragmatic enough to cooperate with the humans.
entries.notes: CONTESTED. Wiki page title is 'Vrlitwhai Kridanik' with DYRL alias 'Vrlitwhai 7018'; en.wikipedia DYRL cast and AniDB also use 'Vrlitwhai 7018'. 'Britai' is the widespread fan/Robotech/phonetic spelling (wiki says 'pronounced Britai Kridanik'; the wiki itself also uses 'Britai Kridanik' in places). Per the wiki-wins rule: 'Vrlitwhai 7018'. If the project prefers readability, 'Britai 7018' is the only acceptable alternative; be consistent with ブリタイ艦.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Zentradi chief archivist / adviser serving under Vrlitwhai.
entries.personality: Analytical, logical and encyclopedic; deeply curious about (and baffled by) human culture.
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Exsedol Folmo' (TV name); DYRL name 'Exsedol 4970' per the same page and en.wikipedia. Variants: 'Exedol' (ADV subs, Robotech 'Exedore'), 'Ekisedoru' (romaji). 'Ekesedol' is not attested; do not use.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Supreme commander of the Zentradi main fleet; main antagonist of DYRL.
entries.personality: Ancient, imposing and absolute; views culture as contamination to be wiped out.
entries.notes: Wiki page title and en.wikipedia use 'Golg Boddole Zer'; the wiki body/nihongo template writes 'Gol Boddole Zer' (closer to ゴル). ADV subs: 'Bodolzaa'. Robotech 'Dolza' must not be used. Default 'Golg Boddole Zer' (title wins); short 'Boddole Zer' (Akurasu flow chart: 'Defeat Boddole Zer').

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Idol singer aboard the Macross; her songs (culture) are the key to defeating the Zentradi.
entries.personality: Bright, cheerful and ambitious pop idol, somewhat self-absorbed; infatuated with Hikaru.
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Lynn Minmay' (romaji 'Rin Minmei'; 'Minmei' is an older variant). No short label given in the brief; 'Minmay' if needed.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Generic Zentradi rank-and-file speaker.
entries.notes: Wiki spelling 'Zentradi' (not Robotech 'Zentraedi').

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Generic Zentradi officer speaker.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Generic Zentradi ship captain speaker.
entries.notes: The game spells it ゼンドラーディ (with ド) here, a typo/variant of ゼントラーディ. Normalize to 'Zentradi' in English; do not reproduce the typo.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Generic female Zentradi (Meltrandi) soldier speaker.
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Meltrandi (Faction)'; also 'Meltran' as a short/adjective form.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Race/faction of giant humanoid warriors; main antagonists.
entries.notes: Added for consistency. Variant 'Zentraedi' (Robotech) not used.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Female Zentradi faction, at war with the male Zentradi in DYRL.
entries.notes: Added for consistency (Akurasu flow chart: 'Meltrandi Picket Ships').

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Standard Zentradi mass-production battle pod.
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Regult' (variant 'Reguld'). Robotech 'Tactical Battle Pod' not used.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Zentradi officer/commander battle pod.
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Glaug' (pronounced 'Glaaj').

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Zentradi general-issue powered suit (DYRL design).
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Nousjadeul-Ger (Movie Ver.)'; drop the disambiguator in-game. Akurasu ACE2 flow chart also uses 'Nousjadeul-Ger'.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Meltrandi high-maneuver battle suit; Milia's machine.
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Queadluun-Rau (Movie ver.)'; drop disambiguator. NOT 'Queadluun-Rhea': that is a separate modernized descendant (クアドラン・レア) from Macross Frontier. Akurasu writes 'Queadluun Rau' without hyphen.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: U.N. Spacy VF-1 variable fighter series.
entries.notes: Wiki title 'VF-1 Valkyrie'. In-game variants per Akurasu: VF-1A Valkyrie, VF-1A Super Valkyrie, VF-1J Valkyrie, VF-1S Valkyrie, VF-1S Strike Valkyrie, Armored Valkyrie.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: SDF-1 Macross, the U.N. Spacy super-dimensional fortress (human flagship).
entries.notes: Wiki title 'SDF-1 Macross'. The game says just マクロス, so use 'Macross' (or 'SDF-1 Macross' where a formal name is needed).

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Vrlitwhai's fleet command battleship.
entries.notes: Descriptive translation; follows whatever is chosen for ブリタイ7018 ('Britai's Ship' if Britai is used). The wiki lists his vessel as a Nupetiet-Vergnitzs-class fleet command battleship (class page documents the TV version). 'Vrlitwhai's Flagship' is also fine.

entries.series: Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.role: Boddole Zer's gigantic mobile-fortress flagship (DYRL final boss).
entries.notes: Wiki title 'Gol Boddole Zer-class' ('commonly referred as Boddole Zer-class'). ボドル is a game abbreviation (Akurasu flow chart: 'Intercept Boddole Fleet'). Alternative: 'Boddole Zer Flagship'.

entries.ja: タック・ケプフォード
entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: ACE2 protagonist; UCE squad leader (First Lieutenant) and Gun Ark test pilot, joins the Albion unit.
entries.personality: Skilled ace and natural leader, but clumsy with machines (mechanically inept); grows suspicious of the Rainen Project and fights to bring Marina back.
entries.notes: SRW wiki page title 'Tak Kepford'; also Akurasu, en.wikipedia, TV Tropes. 'Tuck'/'Tack' are not attested in English sources. VA Daisuke Kishio.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: ACE2 heroine; Ensign in Tak's squad, pilot of the red Gun Ark; goes missing at Torrington Base, reappears with the Rainen Project in the Buster Ark, later rejoins Tak.
entries.personality: Cool and reserved ('defrosting ice queen' in flashbacks); deeply bonded with Tak.
entries.notes: SRW wiki title 'Marina Carson'. VA Naomi Shindou. Akurasu gives the kana as マリーナ but the English is identical.

entries.ja: フィーデル・バルクホルツ
entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: UCE Design Bureau engineer in charge of Ark-series/Gun Ark development; supports Tak and Marina. Spoiler: secretly the son of Albert Rainen and the treacherous mastermind who gave Marina the Buster Ark; fights in the Feather Ark Custom at the end.
entries.personality: Outwardly a kindly professor-type adviser (sends Tak e-mails); actually vengeful against the UCE for what happened to his father.
entries.notes: CONTESTED, no wiki page title exists (SRW wiki only mentions 'Fidel'). 'Fidel Barkholz' (TV Tropes/Tropedia) vs 'Fidel Barkholtz' (Akurasu character list and unit descriptions, Hardcore Gaming 101); Tropedia also has a one-off typo 'Barkhorst'. Chose Barkholz as the German-natural form of バルクホルツ (-holz); Barkholtz is an equally attested fan spelling. 'Balkholz' would also fit the kana but is unattested. When in doubt this is the entry to have a human decide. 博士 forms ('Dr. Barkholz') follow the same spelling. VA Takeshi Aono.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Same person as Fidel Barkholz (title form).
entries.notes: See Fidel Barkholz for the spelling dispute (Barkholz vs Barkholtz).

entries.ja: アルバート・ライネン
entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Former UCE scientist who warned of alien invasion and led the satellite-cannon defense project (Rainen Project) before being forced out; his name heads the antagonist 'Rainen forces'. Barkholz's father.
entries.personality: Visionary 'ignored expert' embittered by the UCE's dismissal of his warnings.
entries.notes: 'Rainen' per SRW wiki ('Rainen Project') and Akurasu ('Albert Rainen', 'Destroy Rainen's Forces'); TV Tropes/Tropedia use 'Reinen'. Exact nature of the on-screen Rainen (alive vs. name/identity used in connection with his son) was not cleanly verified; a ja.wikipedia summary suggested the real Albert is already dead, but treat that as unconfirmed. VA Yasunori Masutani (per Akurasu).

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Combined speaker label for Tak and Marina speaking together.
entries.notes: Built from the two verified names.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: United Community of Earth: the unified Earth government/military of the ACE setting (Japanese 地球統一機構, also described as 地球統一政府).
entries.notes: Expansion 'United Community of Earth' comes from the SRW wiki ACE (first game) page; ACE2 is a continuity reboot but keeps the UCE acronym. 'United Countries of Earth' is NOT attested. Keep 'UCE' as-is in the text; expand only if a gloss is needed. Note ACE R uses 'UCEF'.

entries.role: Generic UCE soldier speaker.
entries.notes: Generic label; descriptive translation.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Generic UCE officer speaker.
entries.notes: Generic label; descriptive translation.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Generic UCE training instructor (exercise/tutorial missions).
entries.notes: Generic label; the game has 12 exercise missions where this speaker likely appears.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Generic UCE communications/mission operator.
entries.notes: Generic label; descriptive translation.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Generic UCE pilot trainee.
entries.notes: Alternative 'UCE Cadet'.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Generic new UCE soldier.
entries.notes: Alternative 'UCE Rookie'. Keep distinct from 訓練生 (Trainee).

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Generic new soldier.
entries.notes: Plain generic; alternative 'Rookie'.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Generic covert operative/saboteur.
entries.notes: Alternative 'Operative'. Faction not verified (could be a Rainen/enemy infiltrator).

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: In-facility/ship public-address announcement used as a speaker label.
entries.notes: Literal 'in-building broadcast'. Alternatives: 'Intercom', 'PA System', 'Announcement'.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2
entries.role: Generic resistance fighter.
entries.notes: Which resistance is not verified (likely the Earth resistance in the Layzner/Grados or L-Gaim storyline rather than an ACE original). Translation itself is safe.

entries.ja: ライネン・プロジェクト
entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Albert Rainen's anti-invader defense project built around the Guardian satellite cannons and the Ark series.
entries.notes: Added for consistency. SRW wiki 'Rainen Project'; TV Tropes uses 'Reinen'.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Latest Ark-series transforming machine from the UCE Design Bureau; Tak's (and initially Marina's red) unit; can call Guardian satellite strikes.
entries.notes: SRW wiki and Akurasu: 'Gun Ark' (two words). en.wikipedia writes 'Gunark'; TV Tropes 'Gun-Ark'. Use 'Gun Ark'.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: First Ark-series machine; discontinued high-performance Guardian System unit; secret unit playable by Marina.

entries.ja: フェザーアークカスタム
entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Barkholz's customized, greatly strengthened Feather Ark (final boss machine).
entries.notes: Akurasu: 'Feather Ark Custom'.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Modified Gun Ark with an evolving Guardian System and fallen-angel styling; Marina's unit while with the Rainen side.
entries.notes: TV Tropes sometimes 'Buster-Ark'. Use 'Buster Ark'.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: Network of (hundreds of) orbital military satellite cannons of the Rainen Project; Gun Ark/Buster Ark can call it via the Guardian System.
entries.notes: Akurasu: Operation 05 'Military Satellite "Guardian"'; ガーディアンシステム = 'Guardian System'; the attack is 'Guardian' / 'Guardian Attack'.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original)
entries.role: UCE Design Bureau machine line: Feather Ark, Gun Ark, Buster Ark.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original, FromSoftware design)
entries.role: Rainen-series unmanned enemy machine introduced in ACE2.
entries.notes: CONFIRMED ACE2 ORIGINAL (ja.wikipedia: FromSoftware-original 'ライネンシリーズ（ザロム、ザロムD）' introduced in ACE2). English 'Zarom' from Akurasu flow chart only; no dedicated wiki page.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode 2 (original, FromSoftware design)
entries.role: Variant of the Zarom (Rainen series).
entries.notes: CONFIRMED ACE2 ORIGINAL. Akurasu: 'Zarom D' ('Defeat Zarom and Zarom Ds'). Meaning of D unverified.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode series original (FromSoftware design)
entries.role: Unmanned UCE/Federation prototype mobile weapon with a large right-arm cannon; low mobility, heavy artillery.
entries.notes: ACE-SERIES ORIGINAL (FromSoftware) recurring from ACE1, not ACE2-new. Akurasu writes 'Loewe' with umlaut (German 'Loewe' = lion); plain-ASCII form 'Loewe' chosen (variants 'Lowe', 'Leve'). Sister units Krebs/Waage are also German zodiac names (Cancer/Leo/Libra), supporting the German reading.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode series original (FromSoftware design)
entries.role: Unmanned UCE-developed flight-capable artillery machine.
entries.notes: ACE-SERIES ORIGINAL (FromSoftware) recurring from ACE1. No English source found. 'Waage' is an inference: German for Libra/scales, matching sister units Krebs (クレーブス, Cancer) and Loewe (Leo). Romanized alternative 'Vage'.

entries.series: Another Century's Episode series original (Banpresto design)
entries.role: Unmanned aerial fire-support enemy unit (more weapon variety than the Skoll).
entries.notes: ACE-SERIES ORIGINAL (Banpresto Norse-mythology line from ACE1: Risnir, Gnost, Harald, Skoll, Thiassi, Tannthor), not ACE2-new. Akurasu: 'Thiassi' (the giant Thjazi; variants 'Thiazi', 'Thjazi', 'Shiasui').

entries.series: Another Century's Episode series original (Banpresto design)
entries.role: Enhanced Risnir variant with gatling guns and beam cannons (unmanned).
entries.notes: ACE-SERIES ORIGINAL (Banpresto, from ACE1). Akurasu: 'Gnost'.

entries.series: Blue Comet SPT Layzner
entries.role: MF-SL-52C atmospheric mass-production Multi Form (Grados).
entries.notes: NOT an ACE original: Layzner unit. SRW wiki mecha list spells it 'MF-SL-52C Slomco'; 'Solomko' is a common romanization. Defer to the Layzner research agent.

entries.series: Blue Comet SPT Layzner
entries.role: SPT-GK-10U Gradosian SPT (Ahmos Gale's machine per SRW wiki).
entries.notes: NOT an ACE original: Layzner unit. SRW wiki 'SPT-GK-10U Greimkaiser'. Defer to the Layzner research agent.
